newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extend latest rally.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extend latest rally.

text.p: Singapore gas oil extended its latest rally late Thursday afternoon in quiet trading on stronger crude values and regional demand, industry sources said.
"Sentiment is fairly bullish. Nobody is selling it down," one broker said.
January gas oil was traded higher at $32.10 and $32.08 a barrel from late Tuesday's at $31.75/$31.85 per barrel, the broker said.
The market was last quoted at $32.00/$32.20 a barrel
February gas oil traded in the afternoon at $31.00 and $31.10 per barrel up from Tuesday's $30.65/$30.75. It was last quoted at $31.00/$31.15 a barrel.

February Brent crude closed up 20 cents to $23.40 a barrel on Tuesday and January gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) also firmer, gaining $4.00 to close at $215.25 per tonne.
Traders said the higher prices were also due to regional demand with India issuing a second tender to buy diesel for delivery in February.
Purchase tenders were also issued by Sri Lanka and Nepal for both diesel and jet/kerosene.

The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was steady on renewed buying seen from Indonesia with talks that deals were done earlier in the week at around 15-20 cents premium to spot Singapore quotes on a free-on-board basis.
The January regrade traded late Tuesday at $1.75 and $1.80 a barrel, brokers said.
January regrade was last quoted at $1.65/$1.85 a barrel, against Tuesday's $1.55/$1.75, brokers said.
January fuel oil was also talked firmer in quiet trading and was quoted at $$120.50/$121.50 per tonne, up from Tuesday's $119.50/$121.00.
